lead: Concrete alone carries only a limited diagonal tension. When the factored shear V_u exceeds the concrete's shear strength, the beam needs shear reinforcement. Vertical stirrups, or bent-up bars, carry the excess. The designer computes the nominal shear stress τ_v, checks it against the concrete's upper limit τ_c,max, subtracts the concrete contribution V_uc, and sizes stirrups from V_us = 0.87 f_y A_sv d / s_v. The result is a spacing s_v that is practical, safe and within code limits. Every beam in a building or bridge uses this check.
prereq: You need: Chapter 3.1 for τ_v and τ_c, and Unit 2 for the beam section and effective depth.

blocks.text: Shear in a beam is diagonal tension. Chapter 3.1 explains how cracks form and how concrete, aggregate interlock, dowel action and stirrups share the force. The code gives the concrete a design shear strength τc, which depends on the concrete grade and the percentage of tension steel. For a rectangular section, the concrete contribution is Vuc = τc bw d. Here bw is the web width in mm and d is the effective depth in mm. Vuc is in N when τc is in N/mm² (MPa). Divide by 1000 to get kN.
τ<sub>v</sub> = V<sub>u</sub> / (b<sub>w</sub> d); V<sub>uc</sub> = τ<sub>c</sub> b<sub>w</sub> d; V<sub>us</sub> = V<sub>u</sub> − V<sub>uc</sub>
blocks.where: τ<sub>v</sub> is the nominal shear stress in MPa; V<sub>u</sub> is the factored shear in N; b<sub>w</sub> is the web width in mm; d is the effective depth in mm; τ<sub>c</sub> is the concrete design shear strength in MPa; V<sub>uc</sub> is the concrete shear capacity in N; V<sub>us</sub> is the shear carried by steel in N.

blocks.text: The applied factored shear is V<sub>u</sub>. It produces the nominal shear stress τ<sub>v</sub> = V<sub>u</sub> / (b<sub>w</sub> d). Keep V<sub>u</sub> in N in this formula. If τ<sub>v</sub> exceeds τ<sub>c,max</sub>, the web is too thin and must be enlarged; stirrups cannot repair a crushed web. If V<sub>u</sub> is greater than V<sub>uc</sub>, the excess V<sub>us</sub> = V<sub>u</sub> − V<sub>uc</sub> is carried by shear reinforcement. If V<sub>u</sub> is not greater than V<sub>uc</sub>, nominal stirrups are still provided.

Some syllabi call the whole procedure 'design for shear'. They also call the two strengths 'design shear strength with and without shear reinforcement'. The first is τc; the second is τc plus the steel term. Torsion adds another shear stress; it is handled in Chapter 3.3.

Vertical stirrups cross the diagonal crack and carry V<sub>us</sub>. Use two-legged stirrups in narrow beams and four-legged stirrups in wide beams. A<sub>sv</sub> is the total area of all stirrup legs that cross the crack. For two-legged 8 mm stirrups, A<sub>sv</sub> = 2 × 50.3 = 100.6 mm².

items: Compute V<sub>u</sub> from the load combination and find τ<sub>v</sub> = V<sub>u</sub>/(b<sub>w</sub>d).
Check τ<sub>v</sub> ≤ τ<sub>c,max</sub>. If it fails, increase the section; do not proceed with stirrup design.
Find V<sub>uc</sub> = τ<sub>c</sub> b<sub>w</sub> d and the steel demand V<sub>us</sub> = V<sub>u</sub> − V<sub>uc</sub>.
Choose the stirrup diameter and number of legs, then get A<sub>sv</sub>.
Compute s<sub>v</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub> d / V<sub>us</sub>. Use V<sub>us</sub> in N; if V<sub>us</sub> is in kN, multiply it by 1000.
Round s<sub>v</sub> down to a practical value and check the minimum steel and maximum spacing rules.

blocks.text: V<sub>us</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub> d / s<sub>v</sub>; s<sub>v</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub> d / V<sub>us</sub>
blocks.where: V<sub>us</sub> is the shear carried by stirrups in N; f<sub>y</sub> is the characteristic yield strength of steel in MPa; A<sub>sv</sub> is the total area of stirrup legs in mm²; d is the effective depth in mm; s<sub>v</sub> is the stirrup spacing in mm. The factor 0.87 is 1/1.15, the steel partial safety factor.

blocks.text: The spacing formula comes from Vus = 0.87 fy Asv d / sv. fy is in MPa, Asv in mm², d in mm and sv in mm. Stirrup legs must be anchored around the top bars; anchorage is covered in Chapter 3.5.

sections.h3: Minimum steel, maximum spacing and bent-up bars

blocks.text: Even when V<sub>us</sub> is zero or small, the code requires minimum shear reinforcement. It controls cracking, holds the longitudinal bars and gives warning before failure. The usual requirement is A<sub>sv</sub>/(b<sub>w</sub> s<sub>v</sub>) ≥ 0.4/(0.87 f<sub>y</sub>). The left side is the stirrup area per unit length. The right side is the minimum ratio for the steel grade.

blocks.where: A<sub>sv</sub> is the total stirrup leg area in mm²; b<sub>w</sub> is the web width in mm; s<sub>v</sub> is the spacing in mm; f<sub>y</sub> is the steel yield strength in MPa. The ratio is dimensionless.

blocks.text: Maximum spacing is the lesser of 0.75d and 300 mm in the general case. Near curtailment points the rules are tighter; see Chapter 3.6. Detailing rules for cover, bar spacing and stirrup shape are in Chapter 3.7.

items: Bent-up bars inclined at α can carry 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>sv</sub> sin α. The code limits the share they take, and their anchorage must be checked.
Vertical stirrups are preferred in thin webs and in regions of high shear.
If the calculated spacing is 257 mm, round down to 250 mm, not up to 260 mm.

figure.caption: The flow turns V_u into τ_v, checks the concrete limit, and subtracts V_uc to find the steel demand. Notice that the final 250 mm spacing is below the 300 mm maximum.

spec.title: Shear design flow
spec.aria: The design flow takes factored shear to nominal stress, subtracts concrete capacity, and ends with 8 mm stirrups at 250 mm spacing.

examples.question: Design vertical stirrups for a rectangular beam with b = 300 mm, d = 550 mm and factored shear V_u = 180 kN. Use M25 concrete with τ_c = 0.62 MPa and τ_c,max = 3.1 MPa. Use Fe415 steel and two-legged 8 mm stirrups. Find the required spacing and state the spacing to be provided.
steps: Compute the nominal shear stress: τ_v = V_u/(b d) = 180 × 10³ / (300 × 550) = 1.09 MPa.
Check the upper limit: τ_v = 1.09 MPa ≤ τ_c,max = 3.1 MPa. The web is adequate.
Find the concrete shear capacity: V_uc = τ_c b d / 1000 = 0.62 × 300 × 550 / 1000 = 102.3 kN.
Find the shear to be carried by stirrups: V_us = V_u − V_uc = 180 − 102.3 = 77.7 kN.
Area of two-legged 8 mm stirrups: A_sv = 2 × 50.3 = 100.6 mm².
Maximum spacing = min(0.75 × 550, 300) = min(412.5, 300) = 300 mm. The calculated 257.1 mm is below this limit.
Round down to a practical spacing: provide 250 mm. This is below 257.1 mm and below 300 mm, so it is safe.
examples.answer: Provide two-legged 8 mm stirrups at 250 mm centres; τ_v = 1.09 MPa is below τ_c,max = 3.1 MPa and the calculated spacing 257.1 mm is rounded down to 250 mm.
examples.check:
b = 300.0
d = 550.0
Vu_kN = 180.0
tau_c = 0.62
tau_cmax = 3.1
fy = 415.0
tau_v = Vu_kN * 1000 / (b * d)
print(f"{tau_v:.2f}")
Vuc = tau_c * b * d / 1000
print(f"{Vuc:.1f}")
Vus = Vu_kN - Vuc
print(f"{Vus:.1f}")
Asv = 2 * 50.3
print(f"{Asv:.1f}")
sv = 0.87 * fy * Asv * d / (Vus * 1000)
print(f"{sv:.1f}")
max_sv = min(0.75 * d, 300.0)
print(f"{max_sv:.1f}")

traps: Forgetting minimum shear reinforcement when V_us is small or zero. The code still requires stirrups.
Checking only τ_v ≤ τ_c,max and not providing steel for V_u > V_uc. The first check protects the web; the second gives the steel.
Mixing N and kN in the spacing formula. V_us in kN must be multiplied by 1000 before dividing.
Using τ_c,max as the concrete design strength for V_uc. τ_c,max is only the upper crush limit; V_uc uses τ_c.
Rounding the stirrup spacing up. Always round down, and also satisfy the maximum spacing limit.

quiz.q: What does V_us mean in shear design?
quiz.a: V_us is the part of the factored shear carried by shear reinforcement. It is V_u − V_uc, where V_uc is the concrete contribution.

quiz.q: State the general maximum spacing limit for vertical stirrups in a beam.
quiz.a: The spacing must not exceed the lesser of 0.75d and 300 mm in the general case.

quiz.q: Why is τ_v ≤ τ_c,max checked before choosing stirrups?
quiz.a: τ_c,max is the upper limit for diagonal compression in the web. If τ_v exceeds it, the web can crush. A larger section is needed; stirrups cannot repair this.

quiz.q: A beam has b_w = 250 mm, d = 500 mm and V_u = 120 kN. Take τ_c = 0.60 MPa and τ_c,max = 3.0 MPa. Find τ_v, V_uc and V_us.
Use two-legged 8 mm Fe415 stirrups with A_sv = 100.6 mm², d = 500 mm and V_us = 45 kN. Find the required spacing and the spacing to provide, applying the general maximum spacing limit.
A designer finds V_u < V_uc and decides to omit stirrups completely. Give two reasons this is unsafe.
quiz.a: The code requires minimum shear reinforcement even when V_u is below V_uc. Concrete shear strength is variable, cracks can form from restrained shrinkage or overload, and stirrups hold the longitudinal bars and give warning before a brittle failure.

quiz.q: A calculated stirrup spacing is 320 mm for d = 500 mm. The designer provides 320 mm. What is wrong?
quiz.a: The general maximum spacing is min(0.75 × 500, 300) = 300 mm. A spacing of 320 mm exceeds 300 mm, so it is not allowed. Provide 300 mm or less.

beyond: Not for the exam. Strut-and-tie models are now common for deep beams and pile caps where plane sections do not hold. Nonlinear finite element analysis helps check shear in complex bridge piers. Fibre-reinforced concrete and high-strength stirrups are active research areas. Search for 'strut-and-tie model', 'shear friction' and 'IS 456 shear design' to go further.
